authorities.name: Carlill v Carbolic Smoke Ball Company
authorities.citation_note: Also commonly cited as [1892] EWCA Civ 1 / [1892] 2 QB 484 - not independently re-confirmed against BAILII this session.
authorities.date_note: Decision date not independently re-confirmed this session; recorded per general corroboration.
authorities.proposition: An advertisement offering a reward for performing a specified act can constitute a binding unilateral offer, accepted by performance of the act itself, without the offeree needing to communicate acceptance in advance; once a promisee acts on such an offer, the promisor cannot revoke it.
authorities.verification_note: Not read directly - BAILII blocked (HTTP 403), block treated as final, no workaround used. Confirmed via Soulsbury v Soulsbury [2007] EWCA Civ 969 (below), fetched live.

authorities.name: Soulsbury v Soulsbury
authorities.proposition: Longmore LJ, para 49: describes the dispute as 'a classic unilateral contract of the Carlill v Carbolic Smoke Ball [1893] 1 QB 256 ... kind,' citing it approvingly, without qualification, 114 years after decision.

edges.verified_via: Soulsbury v Soulsbury [2007] EWCA Civ 969, para 49, fetched directly from Find Case Law: cites Carlill approvingly as the paradigm unilateral-contract authority.

what_this_is_not: One verified node-pair confirming Carlill remains the accepted paradigm authority as of 2007.
